executive_summary.text: Q2 2025 shows mixed performance. Instagram reach fell 9.5% QoQ while Facebook views rose 20.3% and interactions 44.4%. Publications increased 28.6% YoY but fell 25% QoQ. KPI reporting remained steady at 37 recorded items, yet new research staff dropped sharply. Open‑access share stayed high at 96.3%.

key_findings.statement: Instagram reach declined 9.5% QoQ to 7,212, whereas Facebook views grew 20.3% QoQ to 8,135.
Total publications fell 25% QoQ to 27 but were 28.6% higher YoY at 27 versus 21 in Q2 2024.
KPI reporting remained unchanged at 37 recorded items, while new research staff decreased 87.5% QoQ to 1.

kpi_analysis.interpretation: Poster presentations rose 88.9% QoQ to 17, indicating increased dissemination activity.
Publications increased 28% QoQ to 32, reflecting higher research output.
New research staff fell 87.5% QoQ to 1, suggesting a staffing risk.
Funding secured dropped 73.2% QoQ to €1 million, indicating reduced external funding success.
External collaborations rose 200% QoQ to 6, showing expanding partnership activity.
Conference‑related awards fell to zero, a decline in peer‑esteem recognitions.

kpis.summary: KPI reporting stable but several indicators show sharp changes.

findings.statement: New research staff fell to 1, an 87.5% drop QoQ.

trends.statement: Social media performance diverged: Instagram reach declined while Facebook engagement increased.

cross_dataset.statement: Increase in external collaborations (KPI 1.1) coincided with higher poster presentations (KPI 1.6).

risks.statement: Sharp drop in new research staff (−87.5% QoQ) may limit capacity for future projects.
Funding secured fell 73.2% QoQ, potentially constraining research activities.

opportunities.statement: Growth in external collaborations (+200% QoQ) offers potential for new joint initiatives.
High open‑access publication share (96.3%) can be leveraged to enhance visibility and impact.

recommendations.recommendation: Review staffing pipeline and consider targeted recruitment to address the decline in new research staff.
recommendations.reasoning: Stabilising staff numbers is essential for maintaining research output.
recommendations.expected_benefit: Mitigate capacity risk and support future publication growth.

recommendations.recommendation: Develop a strategy to sustain and expand Facebook engagement, building on the 44.4% rise in interactions.
recommendations.reasoning: Leveraging the platform where audience response is improving can boost overall outreach.

recommendations.recommendation: Explore additional funding sources to offset the 73.2% drop in secured funding.
recommendations.reasoning: Diversifying funding streams can reduce reliance on declining sources.
recommendations.expected_benefit: Stabilise financial base for research projects.

best_performing.statement: Facebook interactions (+44.4% QoQ) and visits (+12.9% QoQ) were the strongest social media gains.
